doc.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Worst and best gigs, South Pacific as Bloody Mary
summary: A bad New Year's gig, then her love of playing Bloody Mary in South Pacific on a Midwest tour.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: This is a hard question but I’ll try it. Do you recall any of the worst gigs you ever had to play?

I’m trying to think. I think after, even if they’re the worst after you can laugh about it, so they turn into something that’s not the worst gig. I know that sometimes on New Year’s Eve can be some of the worst gigs. I remember working in a club where there was nowhere to sit. I had to sit on the bench with the organ player ,with the organist, and there wasn’t anywhere for the performers to sit.
Okay. How about the best gigs? A couple of the best gigs you ever had.
Well as I said, I loved working in “South Pacific” for some reason. I loved “South Pacific,” being Bloody Mary. And of course the show had a message so that was even more of a plus.
What was the song that you got to sing as Bloody Mary?

There was two [sings] Talkin’ talkin’ happy talk; and then my favorite one was [sings] Most people live on a lonely island/Lost in the middle of a foggy sea/Most people long for another/I wonder where they wish/They long to be/Bali hai/May call you. Yeah I love that song. Maybe that’s why I loved it so much, I love “Bali Hai.” It’s magical. And a big cast, a huge cast, and it was fun. But I’m sure I’ve had better gigs and I’ve had as much fun, but that one always resonates with me.
And what theater was that in?
We did a Midwest tour of it, but ended up in a dinner theater in Nanuet.

Nanuet, New York. But we started out in Muni Opera, which was outdoors sometimes, and I remember the big trees, huge stage, and you opened your mouth and the bugs were flying in al of us in the cast. I think Giorgio Tozzi and Florence Henderson, and we all were complaining about the bugs. Then we went to Indianapolis and the Starlight Theater, another Starlight Theater. But we ended up in Nanuet, New York.
Julius — that was a different one.
Now you said the Muni Opera?
The Muni Opera is a huge — I guess it’s from municipal opera. I’m not sure if it’s run by the city of St. Louis. It’s a huge venue in a park.
And you probably would have had a fairly large pit orchestra in those days.
